# How we work

## Roles

| Role | Who | Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|
| **Owner** | The human product owner | Approves plans, answers open questions, requests reviews, merges PRs, runs demos |
| **Builder** | Claude Code in VS Code | Implements one task at a time with tests, keeps docs current, opens PRs, addresses review findings |
| **Reviewer** | Claude in the claude.ai "MSP" project | Reviews every PR, writes upcoming slice specs, guards architecture, runs slice reviews |

The builder never merges its own work. The reviewer never pushes to feature branches it didn't create. The owner
has the final say; architectural disagreements become ADRs.

## The task loop

```text
/next-task  ──► plan (plan mode) ──► owner approves ──► implement + test ──► /finish-task (opens PR)
     ▲                                                                              │
     │                                                       owner: "review PR #N" to the reviewer
     │                                                                              ▼
  /clear ◄── owner merges ◄── reviewer approves ◄── /address-review N ◄── reviewer posts findings
```

1. **`/next-task`** — reads docs/build/PROGRESS.md, the roadmap and the current slice spec; picks the next task;
   checks the working tree is clean and `main` is up to date; creates the branch; writes a plan and **stops for
   approval** (in VS Code, use Plan mode or `/plan`; the owner can comment inline on the plan).
2. **Implement** in small commits. Run the relevant tests often; run the full suite before finishing.
3. **`/finish-task`** — builds, formats, lints, runs all tests (incl. architecture and isolation tests),
   regenerates catalogues/OpenAPI/client, runs the `pr-prereviewer` subagent on the diff, fixes real gaps,
   updates PROGRESS.md, commits, pushes and opens the PR with the template filled in.
4. The owner asks the reviewer: "Review PR #N" (docs/build/review-protocol.md).
5. **`/address-review N`** — the builder reads the review (PR comments or pasted text), fixes or answers each
   finding, pushes, and replies on the PR.
6. The reviewer re-reviews the changes; the owner merges (merge commit) and deletes the branch.
7. **`/clear`** before the next task.

## Branches, commits, pull requests

- Branch: `s05/t03-additive-engine` (slice / task-number-slug).
- Commits: Conventional Commits with module scopes — `feat(config): add ADDITIVE scoring engine`,
  `test(operations): …`, `docs: …`, `chore(ci): …`.
- PR title: `[S05-T03] ADDITIVE scoring engine`. Body: .github/pull_request_template.md.
- **Size:** aim for ≤ 600 changed lines excluding generated files, migrations, lockfiles and snapshots. If a task
  will be bigger, propose a split to the owner before starting.
- `main` must always build and pass CI. Merge commits only (no squash or rebase; owner, 2026-10-18). For
  stacked PRs, retarget the next PR to `main` before merging it.
- **Never:** commit to `main`; force-push; merge your own PR; edit a migration that is on `main`; edit
  `docs/reference/`; rewrite an Accepted ADR; disable or skip tests to get green.

## Sessions and context hygiene

- One task per session. `/clear` between tasks. A fresh session with a precise prompt beats a long one full of
  corrections.
- Start by reading the "Now" section of PROGRESS.md and the task's spec — not the whole docs folder.
- Use subagents for broad exploration ("use a subagent to find how tenant filters are applied") so the main
  context stays focused.
- If the owner corrects the same issue twice, stop, summarise what was learned, and suggest a fresh session.

## When to stop and ask (use AskUserQuestion)

- The spec is ambiguous, contradicts an ADR or architecture doc, or can't be met as written.
- The change would cross module ownership, add infrastructure, add a dependency (licence check, ADR-0013), or
  change a published contract, event version or merged migration.
- A test fails and you can't explain why after two attempts.
- You're about to fake data to make something look complete (AR-30).

Unanswered questions go to docs/build/open-questions.md and the task pauses at a safe point.

## Deviations

A deviation from the spec is allowed only after the owner agrees. Record it in the PR's "Deviations" section and
in PROGRESS.md's log. If it changes architecture, propose an ADR (`/new-adr`).

## Keeping docs alive

- Behaviour change → update the relevant docs in the same PR (architecture, domain, UX).
- Generated docs (docs/generated/*, contracts/*) are regenerated by the CLI in `/finish-task` — never hand-edited.
- PROGRESS.md is updated at the end of every task; the roadmap status when a slice completes.

## Local prerequisites

Git · GitHub CLI (`gh auth login`) · .NET 10 SDK · Node.js 24 LTS with pnpm (`corepack enable`) · Docker Desktop
(or Docker Engine + Compose) · VS Code with the Claude Code extension. Optional: the standalone Claude Code CLI
for CLI-only features. On Windows, install Git for Windows (Git Bash) and use Docker Desktop with WSL 2.
